threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 56 bus will get you anywhere on time. Locals know to plan their life around unpredictable delays.
Heard a guy on the N37 loudly claiming he's the 'king of Brixton'—then half an hour later, he couldn’t even find his wallet.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the kebab shop guy remembered my order, and the grandma at the corner bakery saved me her last Brezel. That's when it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find street art that not only covers walls but embraces old abandoned factories, turning them into open-air galleries.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local brings their own bag for tacos at Taqueria La Cumbre—seriously, the takeout containers are a tragedy waiting to happen.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni with a street musician belting out 'I Will Survive' while a guy in a tuxedo tried to tap dance. Pure Tenderloin chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí. But the real vibe is in the quiet plazas where locals sip vermut and chat, far from the tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they stand at the metro ticket machines, staring at the screen like it’s a foreign language. Classic rookie move.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stand bewildered at the number of local coffee shops, trying to choose between flat whites and oat lattes like it’s life or death.
Caught a glimpse of a guy on the night bus perfectly balancing a half-eaten kebab while chatting up a girl. Only in Deptford, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I spotted the same dog in a beret every morning at the corner bakery. That quirky routine made it feel like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg's late-night Döner shops serve their kebabs with curry powder—never seen that in Istanbul or anywhere else. Totally Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You notice they call it 'the Mission' not 'the Mission District' and can name three taquerias that aren't on tourist lists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy making a origami crane from a bus transfer while his toddler watched, totally unbothered by the chaos around him. Classic Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think they can just stroll into a local bar and order a 'tapa' without knowing it's actually a 'pica-pica' in our part of town.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still navigate the metro with a paper map, oblivious to the efficiency of Google Maps—classic sign of a newbie in Gràcia.
